$comment: Source of truth for the Cloudflare MCP portal mapping of server `seerrsense` (mctlhq/.github#35). Every tool this server registers must appear here with an explicit decision; tests/portal-allowlist.test.ts fails the build otherwise. An enabled tool must carry a `reason` that says what it exposes or changes and why that is acceptable on a shared surface — a write tool must additionally be named in writeToolsOnPortal in that test. Apply with the same operator-run flow as the other upstreams (mctl-telegram scripts/portal-allowlist-apply.sh, one file per server).

tools.name: whoami
tools.reason: Returns who the session is authenticated as and whose Seerr it reaches; reads nothing from the catalogue and names no title.

tools.name: search_media
tools.reason: Searches the household's catalogue by title and returns TMDB matches; exposes what the connected Seerr can see, not what anyone watched.

tools.name: resolve_media
tools.reason: Resolves a title to a single TMDB id, returning the same catalogue-shaped data as search_media and no viewing history.

tools.name: get_media
tools.reason: Returns one title's availability and request state in the household's Seerr; catalogue metadata, no personal viewing data.

tools.name: request_media
tools.reason: Files a request in the household's own Overseerr or Jellyseerr, which fetches media and consumes their storage and bandwidth. Enabled on the shared portal by owner decision 2026-09-12 (mctlhq/.github#35): the portal decides visibility, and the tool's own seerr:request scope check decides whether the request is actually filed.
